text: Iterative Magnitude Pruning (IMP) applied to mean-field variational Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) trained on the CIFAR10 image classification dataset produces sparse subnetworks (mask-plus-original-initialization pairs) that match or in some cases surpass the dense unpruned Bayesian model's test accuracy across ResNet-18, VGG11, and ViT-tiny for a wide sparsity range, with performance degradation appearing only beyond ≈98% sparsity or at the extreme final level where ≈1.2% of parameters remain.

Across the evaluated architectures (Vision Transformer (ViT)) on the CIFAR10 dataset, in winning tickets found through iterative magnitude pruning, ResNet and VGG retain earlier-layer parameters more strongly than the ViT.
Increasing model size across ResNet-110, VGG19, and ViT-base improves absolute test accuracy of both deterministic and Bayesian models.
